_comment: SHARED FIXTURE (NRM-4) — two independent implementations must agree on this document.
Rust  : nmts/crypto/tests/api.rs            (what the standalone recovery tool parses)
Web   : nmts/web/test/recovery-map.test.ts  (what the browser writes)
Keys beginning with _ are documentation and are ignored by both parsers.
WHAT NRM-4 ADDS: padded_len, on a part whose stored stream was sealed LARGER than the bytes
it contributes, so that nobody who can see the stored object can read the file's real size
off it. The padding is inside the plaintext, before sealing, because an NCF-3 header is
authenticated but NOT encrypted: plaintext_len sits in the clear at offset 16 of a public
Walrus object, so padding tacked onto the stored bytes would leave the true length legible.
WHY TWO NUMBERS RATHER THAN ONE: plaintext_len keeps its old meaning — the real bytes this
part contributes — so 'the parts must sum to exactly size' keeps its exact strength. Folding
padding into it would turn that equality into 'at least', which accepts any size below the
real one and hands back a truncated file with nothing to say so.
BOTH SIDES MUST REFUSE: padded_len in a document declaring v < 4, and padded_len that is not
strictly greater than plaintext_len (equal is written as absence; smaller is impossible).
The AMOUNT of padding is deliberately unchecked — it follows a setting a person can change,
so a rule here would refuse files padded under a setting this build has not heard of.
The two items are the two shapes an upload produces: a small file sitting on the 1 MiB
floor (12 real bytes inside a 1 MiB stream), and a multi-part file whose FULL parts are
untouched and whose TAIL is padded.
